title: Procedure header declares its kind; validate registry against headers (S)
description:
Only email_submission_processor.tac declares '-- papyrus-procedure-kind: …'. Kinds and filenames disagree elsewhere (newsroom.reporting.context → reporter.tac; newsroom.research.explorer → research_explorer.tac), and nothing checks that a registered kind points at the right procedure.

Fix:
- Every procedure's first line declares its kind.
- At load and in CI, check that each registry entry's file declares the same kind.
- Check that no two files declare the same kind.
- Check that every CLI command in requiredCliProcedures resolves.

Acceptance: a CI check that fails on any mismatch, with unit tests for each failure case.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Built and merged to develop (PR #1643). Every procedure file declares its kind on its first line (14 files; kinds newsroom.copywriter, newsroom.editor and newsroom.researcher were coined, the other 11 existed). papyrus-required-procedures.json gained a procedures map (kind to file). papyrus_content/procedure_registry.py reports: a file with no kind, two files with one kind, a registry entry whose file is missing or declares another kind, a file the registry does not list, and a CLI command whose kind has no entry. python -m papyrus_content.procedure_registry is a CI step in python-checks, and procedures seed-required runs it first and reads file paths from the registry (the hardcoded dict is gone). Specs: features_backend/procedure-registry.feature (10 scenarios), procedure_registry_test.py (18 tests). Not done: nothing in scope; moving the files into the wheel is PPY-e95a0c (PR #1646).
